title: Why coffee prices swing: supply sits in a few tropical origins
description: A frost in one country or a drought in another can move the whole world price. No price data is shown here — only where the beans come from.

source.name: Geographic references from Natural Earth (qualitative explainer)

markers.label: Brazil — Minas Gerais
markers.note: The world's largest producer. A single frost or drought in this belt sends Arabica futures soaring — the biggest swing factor of all.

markers.label: Vietnam — Central Highlands
markers.note: The dominant Robusta origin. Drought here tightens the cheaper end of the market that instant coffee depends on.

markers.label: Colombia
markers.note: A benchmark washed-Arabica origin; heavy rain in La Niña years cuts yields and quality.

markers.label: Ethiopia
markers.note: Arabica's birthplace and a major specialty origin; political and logistics shocks ripple into premiums.

markers.label: Indonesia — Sumatra
markers.note: A large Robusta producer straddling the equator, exposed to the same monsoon swings as Vietnam.
